overview: Nanshan Aluminium International is a Cayman-incorporated, Hong Kong-listed (IPO 25 March 2025) producer of metallurgical-grade alumina, operating a single large refinery complex (PT. Bintan Alumina Indonesia, "BAI") in the Galang Batang Special Economic Zone on Bintan Island, Indonesia, with 4 million tonnes/year of designed capacity after completing its New Alumina Production Project in 2025. The company sells alumina to regional downstream smelters and global commodity traders across Southeast and South Asia, and is now building a first-phase 250,000 tonne/year electrolytic (primary) aluminium smelter to move downstream. Its controlling shareholder is Shandong Nanshan Aluminium Co., Ltd. (600219.SH), part of China's Nanshan Group conglomerate; Malaysian smelter group Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Berhad is a major strategic shareholder (~20.6%) via its historic stake in BAI.

business_model.summary: Single operating segment: production and sale of metallurgical-grade alumina (plus small aluminium hydroxide volumes), priced on formula-based contracts referencing published market indices (LME/Platts) or via spot bidding. Revenue is a function of sales volume (ramping sharply as the 4Mt capacity came fully online through 2025) multiplied by average selling price (ASP), which tracks volatile international alumina index prices. No long-term fixed-price contracts insulate the company from commodity swings. The business is commodity/cyclical and transactional rather than recurring, though customer relationships are described as long-term and stable.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — regional downstream aluminium smelters and global commodity trading houses; customer base diversifying (new India-based manufacturer customer added in FY2025; Hong Kong, Malaysia, Switzerland, Singapore, US and Indonesia among top revenue geographies by customer domicile)
business_model.geographic_mix: Production 100% Indonesia (Bintan Island). FY2025 revenue by customer domicile: Hong Kong 38%, Malaysia 37%, India 13%, Switzerland 6%, Singapore 4%, other (US, Indonesia) ~2%. Geographic revenue mix reflects trading-hub domiciles of customers, not necessarily end-use location.

main_competitors: Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Berhad (shareholder and offtake partner, also a smelter competitor/customer)

Chinese and other Southeast Asian/global alumina refiners (e.g., South32, Alcoa, Rio Tinto on a global scale; Indonesian refinery entrants such as Inalum/PT Well Harvest Winning and other new Bintan/Kalimantan projects)
Indonesian domestic bauxite/alumina new entrants expanding capacity (adding to regional oversupply)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest single-site alumina producers in Southeast Asia by designed capacity (4 million tonnes/year), newly scaled up from 2 million tonnes in 2024; a relatively small share of the global alumina market (~150Mt/year) but a significant regional supplier serving Southeast/South Asian smelters.

moat_factors.factor: Low-cost Bayer-process production tied to local bauxite
moat_factors.description: Co-located bauxite resource access in Indonesia and self-owned deep-water port (70,000-ton berth plus smaller berths) lower logistics and input costs versus importers.

4Mt designed capacity and established infrastructure give scale advantages versus newer, smaller entrants, though Indonesia's refinery pipeline (potential ~30Mt capacity) threatens to erode this over time.

Backing from Nanshan Group (China) and Press Metal (Malaysia, a major downstream smelter) provides offtake relationships, technical know-how and capital access, though it is also a related-party concentration risk.
Planned downstream move into electrolytic aluminium (250kt phase 1, 500kt planned) could internalize margin and reduce alumina price-cycle exposure, but is unproven and years from commissioning.
Alumina is a commoditized input priced off public indices; minimal product differentiation or customer lock-in beyond logistics convenience.

weaknesses: Single-product, single-site concentration — all production from one Indonesian complex, creating operational, geological, political and weather-related concentration risk

No pricing power — alumina is sold at formula/index-linked or spot-bid prices, so margins are fully exposed to the global alumina price cycle, as shown by the ASP collapse from $529/t (H1 FY2025) to $320/t (H1 FY2026) and gross margin falling from ~53% to 15.8%
Heavy reliance on continued access to Indonesian bauxite under a government quota (RKAB) system that has periodically constrained supply industry-wide
New, unproven in the downstream electrolytic aluminium business, a different cost structure (very power-intensive) and competitive set
Governance structure concentrates power in one executive (Chairman and CEO combined in Mr. Hao Weisong, a deviation from the HK Corporate Governance Code)
Majority ownership and key supply/customer relationships sit with related parties (Nanshan Group, Press Metal), raising related-party transaction and minority-shareholder governance considerations

growth_drivers: Electrolytic Aluminium Project — first phase 250,000 tonnes/year smelter in Indonesia, ~US$436.6 million estimated investment over ~2 years, construction initiated in 2026, intended to create a second growth curve and internalize the alumina-to-metal value chain

Further planned expansion of electrolytic aluminium capacity by an additional 500,000 tonnes/year in the medium-to-long term, aiming to eventually match alumina capacity with downstream smelting capacity

Full ramp of the 4 million tonne alumina capacity (both 1Mt phases of the New Alumina Production Project only reached full run-rate in Q3/Q4 2025), supporting further volume growth even as prices are weak
Customer base diversification — new sales relationships in India and other non-traditional markets, reducing reliance on a few trading hubs
Structural secular tailwind: Southeast Asian aluminium demand growth from regional economic growth, population increases and infrastructure development

Potential supply-demand rebalancing in alumina as new capacity (including the Group's own) gets absorbed by lagging downstream electrolytic aluminium capacity; management also cites a structurally tight long-term outlook for electrolytic aluminium amid China's production cap
Possible further upstream/downstream integration ('full industry chain' ambition covering bauxite mining through downstream processing) within the Galang Batang Special Economic Zone

business.description: All alumina output comes from one Indonesian complex; any operational disruption (plant outage, labour, logistics, weather) would hit the entire business.

ASP fell ~39.5% H1 FY2026 vs H1 FY2025 ($529/t to $320/t), driving gross margin down from ~53% to 15.8%; prices are set by volatile global indices (LME/Platts) with no hedging of the underlying commodity.

Revenue is concentrated in a handful of geographic trading hubs (Hong Kong, Malaysia) and large commodity traders/smelters; loss of a key relationship (including Press Metal, a related party) could be material.

business.risk: Execution risk on Electrolytic Aluminium Project
business.description: New product line, new cost structure (power-intensive smelting), ~$436.6m capex and ~2-year build; cost overruns, delays, or a weak metal price environment at commissioning could depress returns.

financial.description: FY2025 capex ($392.2m) exceeded operating cash flow ($359.7m), producing negative free cash flow (-$32.4m); further heavy capex for the smelter project will continue to pressure FCF even though the company holds a large net cash position.

Revenue mostly USD-denominated but costs are USD-denominated-yet-settled in Indonesian Rupiah; dividends/capex flows also cross into HKD and RMB; the company held no currency hedges as of H1 FY2026 (down from using forward contracts in FY2025).
OECD Pillar Two top-up tax rules (adopted by Indonesia, Hong Kong, Singapore) added ~US$50.2 million to FY2025 tax expense and could continue to raise the effective tax rate going forward.
Dividend payout fell sharply (H1 FY2026 interim dividend HK$0.16/share vs HK$0.65/share prior year) in line with the profit decline, showing dividends are not protected from the commodity cycle.

regulatory.description: Indonesia's annual mining work-plan approval mechanism tightened bauxite supply industry-wide in H1 FY2026, raising raw material cost/availability risk even though the company sources mainly through local purchasing rather than owned mining concessions.

regulatory.risk: Indonesian resource nationalism / export and investment policy
regulatory.description: Indonesia has a history of shifting bauxite/mineral export and downstream-processing mandates; future policy changes could affect feedstock costs, permitting for the new smelter, or royalty/tax terms.

regulatory.risk: China/Nanshan Group relationship and related-party transactions
regulatory.description: Controlling shareholder is a PRC-listed Nanshan Group entity; related-party supply, service or financing arrangements with Nanshan Group/Nanshan Aluminium and with Press Metal require ongoing governance scrutiny, and geopolitical friction affecting PRC-linked companies' access to HK/international capital markets is a tail risk.
Electrolytic aluminium smelting is energy- and emissions-intensive; environmental and power-supply approvals in Indonesia could delay the new project.

macro.description: S&P Global and other analysts forecast a continued global alumina surplus (~1.2-1.8 million tonnes in 2026) following a wave of new refinery capacity (including the Group's own and other Indonesian/Chinese entrants), keeping prices depressed near multi-year lows (~US$300-350/t range through much of 2026).
China's electrolytic aluminium capacity cap and domestic alumina supply/demand dynamics heavily influence global alumina and metal prices, which the Group cannot control.
Management explicitly flags escalating geopolitical tensions, global trade conflicts and supply-chain disruption as uncertainties affecting outlook.

Coal, caustic soda and electricity costs are key inputs for Bayer-process alumina production (and will be even more critical for the power-hungry smelter); cost per tonne held 'relatively stable' recently but is sensitive to energy markets.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global alumina market is in a cyclical oversupply phase (forecast surplus of roughly 1.2-1.8 million tonnes in 2026), driven in large part by new Indonesian and Chinese refinery capacity (including the Group's own 4Mt ramp-up), pressuring prices from the 2024-2025 highs (~US$430-535/t) down toward the ~US$300-350/t range through 2026. A rebound in international alumina prices to ~US$348/t was noted in August 2026, which management describes as 'bottoming out,' with a positive medium-term view predicated on electrolytic aluminium capacity (demand for alumina) eventually catching up with new alumina supply. Southeast Asia's aluminium/alumina demand is supported by longer-term secular growth in regional infrastructure, construction, transport and electrification.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — a pure-play commodity producer whose revenue and margins swing directly with a volatile, globally-traded index price (LME/Platts alumina) with no fixed-price contracts or hedges on the commodity itself.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no borrowings, net cash position of ~$666.7 million at June 2026); indirect sensitivity via global growth/demand for aluminium-intensive goods and via capital markets access for the smelter project funding.
key_input_costs: Bauxite (subject to Indonesian RKAB mining quotas)
Electricity (increasingly critical for planned electrolytic aluminium smelting)

recent_developments.event: Announced the Electrolytic Aluminium Project — first phase 250,000 tonnes/year, ~US$436.57 million estimated investment over ~2 years, plus planning for an additional 500,000 tonnes/year in the medium-to-long term.

Completed a top-up Placing and Subscription: 31,000,000 existing shares placed by the controlling shareholder at HK$64.50/share, with an equal number of new shares issued to the vendor; net proceeds ~HK$1,986.76 million (~US$256 million), ~90% earmarked for the Electrolytic Aluminium Project and ~10% for working capital.
New Alumina Production Project's two 1-million-tonne phases both commissioned (Q3 and Q4 2025), lifting designed annual alumina capacity to 4 million tonnes.

FY2025 revenue rose 11.9% to US$1,141.8 million (volume +22.5% to 2.643Mt, offsetting an 8.7% ASP decline to US$432/t), but gross margin fell from 50.6% to 41.9% and net profit fell 8.6% to US$418.1 million, partly due to a ~US$50.2 million Pillar Two top-up tax impact.

Alumina ASP collapsed 39.5% year-on-year to US$320/t; revenue fell 30.5% to US$415.0 million; gross margin fell to 15.8%; profit attributable to shareholders fell 74.8% to US$62.7 million; interim dividend cut to HK$0.16/share from HK$0.65/share.
Tight Indonesian bauxite supply (government RKAB mining work-plan approval constraints) pressured input availability industry-wide during the first half of 2026.
International alumina prices showed signs of bottoming, averaging ~US$348/t for 1-18 August 2026, up from the H1 2026 average of US$307/t, per LME Alumina (Platts) data cited by management.

CICC maintained an Outperform rating but cut its 12-month price target by ~47% to HK$34.81 (and cut 2026/2027 net profit forecasts by 50%/32%) following the weak H1 FY2026 results; broader analyst consensus (per TipRanks) averaged a HK$49.75 target with Buy ratings, though targets vary widely (HK$26-75) reflecting high uncertainty around the alumina price cycle.

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.notes: Funded by internal resources, net proceeds of the January 2026 Placing and Subscription (~90% of ~HK$1,986.76m net proceeds, i.e. ~HK$1,788.08m earmarked), and operating cash flow; expected fully utilised by 31 December 2029 per the placing use-of-proceeds disclosure.

items.target: 500,000 tpa planning (medium-to-long term, no firm capex or timeline disclosed)
items.notes: Stated intention to eventually align electrolytic aluminium capacity with the 4 million tonne alumina capacity; no specific year given.

items.target: 4 million tonnes/year designed capacity, now fully commissioned
items.vs_prior: raised (vs. 2 million tonnes historically, doubled via the New Alumina Production Project completed in 2025)
items.notes: No explicit volume guidance figure given for FY2026, but management expects continued full utilisation of the 4Mt capacity; H1 FY2026 volume already up 15.0% YoY to 1.296Mt despite the weak price environment.

items.vs_prior: lowered (management explicitly flagged downward pressure on revenue and margins from falling international alumina prices, which continued into H1 FY2026)
items.notes: Management noted a price rebound to ~US$348/t in early August 2026 from the H1 average of US$307/t, calling it 'a clear trend of bottoming out,' but gave no formal price or margin target.

items.target: No fixed payout ratio disclosed; FY2025 full-year dividend HK$1.06/share (interim HK$0.65 + final HK$0.41); H1 FY2026 interim dividend HK$0.16/share
items.vs_prior: lowered (H1 FY2026 interim dividend down ~75% YoY, tracking the profit decline)
items.notes: No stated minimum payout ratio; dividends appear to track net profit rather than a fixed policy.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Hao Weisong frames FY2025 as a 'pivotal year' of international expansion (HKEX listing, Hang Seng Composite inclusion, Stock Connect and FTSE index inclusion) and reiterates the strategy to extend the industrial chain from alumina into electrolytic aluminium as the 'second growth curve.' Management explicitly warns that the continuing decline in international alumina prices would pressure revenue and profitability 'particularly in the first half year of 2026' (a warning that proved accurate), while expressing medium-to-long-term confidence that new electrolytic aluminium demand will rebalance the alumina supply-demand picture, and that the structurally tight global electrolytic aluminium market (due to China's production cap) supports the smelter investment case.

bull_case: Vertical integration into electrolytic aluminium (250kt phase 1, 500kt planned) could capture downstream margin, reduce standalone alumina-price-cycle exposure, and open a second growth leg over the next several years

Strong balance sheet — net cash of US$666.7 million, zero borrowings, and freshly raised ~US$256 million from the January 2026 placing give ample capacity to self-fund the smelter buildout without leverage or near-term dilution risk

Scaled-up, low-cost production base — 4 million tonne designed capacity (doubled in 2025) at a single, well-located Indonesian site with its own deep-water port infrastructure, positioning it as one of Southeast Asia's largest alumina producers just as the region's aluminium demand grows structurally

Alumina prices showing early signs of bottoming (August 2026 rebound to ~US$348/t from H1 lows near US$300-307/t), which — combined with still-growing sales volumes — could restore margin expansion if sustained

Backing and alignment of two strategic industry shareholders (Nanshan Group/China Hongqiao-adjacent network and Press Metal, a major Malaysian smelter) provides offtake relationships, technical expertise and credibility that a standalone junior producer would lack
bear_case: Pure commodity exposure with no pricing power — H1 FY2026 showed how fast earnings can collapse (revenue -30.5%, profit -74.8%) when alumina ASP falls, and the global alumina market remains in a forecast multi-million-tonne surplus through 2026 as new Indonesian and Chinese capacity (including the company's own) comes online

Single-site, single-segment concentration risk — the entire business depends on one Indonesian production complex and one product (alumina plus a small by-product stream), with no geographic or product diversification to cushion a local operational or regulatory disruption

Execution and capital-allocation risk on the new electrolytic aluminium project — a ~US$436.6 million-plus capex program in an unfamiliar, power-intensive business line, funded partly from a dilutive placing, with multi-year lead time before any return and exposure to a separate, equally volatile metal price cycle

Indonesian regulatory/resource risk — the government's bauxite mining quota (RKAB) system already constrained raw material supply in H1 FY2026, and broader shifts in Indonesian resource nationalism or permitting could raise costs or delay the smelter

Governance and related-party concentration — combined Chairman/CEO role (a Code deviation), controlling shareholder ties to a PRC-listed Nanshan Group entity, and a major customer/shareholder relationship with Press Metal create related-party and minority-shareholder alignment risks that are hard for outside investors to fully diligence
